items.explanation: Gingrich's Contract nationalized the 1994 House campaign around shrinking 'big government,' and Republicans gained 54 seats to take the House for the first time since 1954 — the electoral payoff of the conservative movement's growth, and the event that made the Contract historically significant.
options: (A) Voter turnout collapsed to historic lows, undermining the results' significance.
(B) Democrats retained control of the House despite the nationalized Republican campaign.
(C) The GOP won its first House majority in 40 years, ending four decades of Democratic control.
(D) A third-party movement captured a decisive bloc of House seats.
items.stem: The 1994 midterm elections that followed the Contract with America most directly demonstrated which of the following?
items.stimulus: The 1994 Contract with America proposed not just policy change but restoring trust between the people and their elected representatives, ending four decades of one-party control of the House with a new majority that would shrink a government described as too big, too intrusive, and too free with the public's money. — paraphrased from the Contract with America, 1994

option_explanations.A: Voter turnout did not collapse in 1994 — it rose from the 1990 midterms, and the results were enormously significant. The election ended forty years of Democratic House control; nothing about the turnout undermines that.
option_explanations.B: The Democrats lost the House in 1994 — that is the whole point of the election's fame. Republicans gained 54 House seats and took the majority for the first time since 1954; the nationalized campaign worked.
option_explanations.C: Correct. The 1994 midterms ended four decades of Democratic control of the House: Republicans, campaigning on Gingrich's Contract with America and its promise to shrink a government described as too big and too intrusive, gained 54 seats and won their first House majority since 1954. It was the electoral payoff of the conservative movement's decades-long growth — and the event that made the Contract historically significant.
option_explanations.D: No third party captured House seats in 1994. Ross Perot's Reform movement won nearly 19 percent of the 1992 presidential vote but elected no one to the House; 1994 was a two-party election in which the Republicans were the winners.

items.explanation: Despite the 1994 rhetoric, federal spending and the scope of government kept growing through the 1990s and 2000s — popular programs (Social Security, Medicare) proved politically untouchable, and even Republican administrations expanded the state.
options: (A) Republicans were shut out of the House, Senate, and presidency for a decade afterward.
(B) Republicans successfully dismantled the core programs of Lyndon Johnson's Great Society.
(C) Even as Republicans denounced 'big government,' the federal government kept growing.
(D) Large numbers of House Republicans defected to the Democratic Party in protest.
items.stem: Which generalization about the Contract with America's aftermath is best supported?

option_explanations.A: Republicans were not shut out — they won both the House and the Senate in 1994 and held Congress for most of the next decade. This describes the opposite of what happened.
option_explanations.B: The core Great Society programs survived the 1994 revolution intact. Medicare, Medicaid, and federal education and antipoverty programs were not dismantled — they proved politically untouchable, and Republicans learned that attacking popular entitlements carried electoral costs (as the 1995–96 government shutdowns showed).
option_explanations.C: Correct. The irony of the post-1994 era is that for all the Contract's denunciations of 'big government,' the federal government kept growing — through the late 1990s and 2000s, under both parties. Popular programs like Social Security and Medicare could not be touched politically, and even Republican administrations expanded the state (the prescription-drug benefit, homeland security, education mandates). Rhetoric shrank government; budgets did not.
option_explanations.D: No such defection occurred. House Republicans did not cross to the Democratic Party in protest after 1994 — the Republican majority held together, and party-switching in this era ran the other direction (southern conservatives joining the GOP).

items.explanation: The Global Exchange declaration's specific demands — trade serving 'equitable and sustainable development' with worker and environmental protections, decided by a body accountable to citizens rather than corporations — show the 'teamsters and turtles' character of the 1999 Seattle WTO protests: an alliance of labor unions, environmentalists, and human-rights advocates against corporate-dominated free trade.
options: (A) They were organized and directed by the United States government.
(B) They united labor, environmental, and human-rights groups in a broad coalition.
(C) They endorsed corporate-led globalization as the path to prosperity.
(D) They demanded an end to all international trade.
items.stem: The declaration's demands — worker and environmental protections in trade deals, and a democratic body accountable to citizens — best illustrate which of the following about the Seattle protests?
items.stimulus: A 1999 Global Exchange declaration, issued around the Seattle WTO protests, charged that the World Trade Organization was dominated by corporate interests and demanded trade policy representing all sectors of society, trade serving equitable and sustainable development with worker and environmental protections, and a democratic body accountable to citizens replacing the WTO. — paraphrased from Global Exchange (Seattle), 'Declaration for Global Democracy,' 1999

option_explanations.A: The Seattle protests were organized against the establishment, not by it. The WTO ministerial was the U.S.-backed event; the tens of thousands in the streets — union members, environmentalists, students — were there to disrupt it. A government-directed protest against a government-hosted trade meeting makes no sense.
option_explanations.B: Correct. The Global Exchange declaration's demands — trade serving 'equitable and sustainable development,' with worker and environmental protections, decided by a democratic body accountable to citizens rather than corporations — capture the 'teamsters and turtles' character of the 1999 Seattle WTO protests: a broad coalition uniting labor unions, environmentalists, and human-rights advocates against corporate-dominated globalization.
option_explanations.C: The declaration attacks corporate-led globalization; it does not endorse it. Its central charge is that the WTO was 'dominated by corporate interests' — the protesters' enemy, not their program.
option_explanations.D: The declaration demands fairer trade, not no trade. Its program is trade with worker and environmental protections, decided democratically — a reformed globalization, not autarky. Ending all international trade was no protester's demand.

items.explanation: Both the anti-globalization movement and the 1960s New Left linked foreign policy to corporate power, demanded democratic participation in decisions made by unaccountable elites, and used mass street protest — a shared critique of concentrated power across three decades.
options: (B) The Bretton Woods agreements (1944) that created the International Monetary Fund.
(C) The New Left's critiques of the Vietnam War in the 1960s.
items.stem: The declaration's political outlook is most similar to which of the following?

option_explanations.A: Wilson's Fourteen Points (1918) were a program of liberal internationalism — open diplomacy, free trade, a League of Nations. The Seattle declaration is skeptical of exactly that kind of elite-managed international order; its demand is for democratic accountability over corporate-dominated institutions, not Wilsonian idealism.
option_explanations.B: The Bretton Woods agreements (1944) created the IMF and the World Bank — the institutional ancestors of the WTO system the Seattle protesters were demonstrating against. The declaration's outlook opposes the Bretton Woods order; it does not resemble it.
option_explanations.C: Correct. Both the anti-globalization movement and the 1960s New Left linked foreign policy to corporate power, demanded democratic participation in decisions made by unaccountable elites, and took their case to the streets in mass protest. The Seattle declaration's charge — that the WTO served corporations rather than citizens — echoes the New Left's charge that the Vietnam-era establishment served power rather than people.
option_explanations.D: The Contract with America (1994) was a conservative program to shrink government and cut regulation — the political opposite of the Seattle declaration's demand for worker and environmental protections in trade deals. One wants less government; the other wants more democratic control over the economy.
